title: What if Harvard moved to California?
narrator: Deadpan documentary: calm and dry, treats the impossible premise like a serious report. The jokes land through understatement.
logline: Harvard Yard moves to Los Angeles. The bricks are older than the freeways, and nobody packed sunscreen.

cues.onScreen: What if Harvard moved to California?
cues.narration: What if Harvard moved to California?

cues.onScreen: Harvard: founded 1636. Brick, ivy, and big libraries.
cues.narration: Harvard: founded 1636. Brick, ivy, and serious libraries.
cues.delivery: Respectful, a little stiff, like a campus tour guide.

cues.onScreen: Boston gets about 49 inches of snow a year.
cues.narration: And about 49 inches of Boston snow a year.

cues.onScreen: Then Harvard Yard pops off the map.
cues.narration: Then Harvard Yard gets packed up, brick by brick.

cues.onScreen: It flies about 4,180 km west to Los Angeles.
cues.narration: About 4,180 km west. Some bricks are older than every freeway they pass.

cues.onScreen: And lands right next to the beach.
cues.narration: It lands a few miles from the beach. Nobody packed sunscreen.

cues.onScreen: Problem 1: The ivy dries out in the sun.
cues.narration: Week one: the ivy dries out. Crimson sweatshirts become optional.

cues.onScreen: Problem 2: Lectures move to the beach.
cues.narration: Week two: lectures move to the beach. Attendance goes up.
cues.delivery: Pleased, as if this is data.

cues.onScreen: Problem 3: UCLA is suddenly a neighbor.
cues.narration: Week three: UCLA is a neighbor. Both sides pretend not to notice.

cues.onScreen: So Harvard gets a California makeover.
cues.narration: First new tradition: complaining about the 405.
cues.delivery: Proud, like announcing a real tradition.

cues.onScreen: Would you trade snow for surf?
cues.narration: Would you trade snow for surf?

notes: 405 is the freeway name (I-405), not a statistic.
